properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BLACKHILL ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/06/2022
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 958086
Permit API: 015-23678
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Springfield Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/06/2022
Comments: Inspection conducted to review site conditions following completions and residual waste processing activities. There are no Blackhill representatives on site at time of inspection. Two vacuum trucks are on location removing fluid from secondary containment of GPUs and produced fluid tanks. Weather conditions are sunny, 73 degrees F. Operator completed flowback operations on site during late winter and spring of 2022. Energy Water Services VOX4 evaporators were used to reduce produced water volumes and concentrate flow-back fluid under EFacts authorization #1379075. One frac tank battery remains on site containing six tanks within secondary containment along the eastern side of the pad. Small earth working equipment remains on site including a mini excavator and skidsteer. Field conductivity screenings were conducted on the Kingsley E pad using an Oakton PCTS 50 meter and a Hanna Groline soil conductivity meter. Salt crystallization was observed in dry puddles and mud between the production fluid tanks and the frac tank battery. Conductivity readings observed within production fluid tank secondary containment were over range (> 20 mS/cm) and puddled water and mud off containment ranged from 3-6.78 mS/cm. Field sample 4406-014 was collected from a puddled water west of the well cellars (photos 7&8). Operator was notified via phone on 6/7/22 of the areas of concern. Additional violations may be issued pending results of water sample analysis.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/11/2024
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8182782
Permit API: 015-23838
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Columbia Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/11/2024
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Repsol's Crank (03-067) O well site located in Columbia Township, Bradford County on 4/11/2024 at 0900 hours. The weather was 56 degrees F with cloudy skies and light rain. Rain fell onsite within the past 24 hours as well. An Act 9 sign is located at the site entrance.The site remains set-up for flow back activities. Crews worked today preparing equipment for site removal and recovering fluids within secondary containments and temporary storage tanks. Secondary containment structures remain in working condition with no evidence of leaking observed. The majority of the areas surrounding the well pad remain permanently stabilized with vegetated cover. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed. Pooled fluids on the pad surface were field measured for electrical conductivity ranging from 570 to 1800us/cm. There was no evidence of spills/releases observed outside of secondary containment. On 3/20/2024, outlined within inspection report #3730668, the DEP observed elevated conductivity fluids pooled on the pad surface field measured at ~5.56mS/cm. Based on the elevated conductivity reading, the DEP collected a sample for standard analysis code 942 (Sample #0983-421). The analytical results from that sample are attached to this inspection report as photos and a file. The findings were reported to Repsol who promptly dispatched an environmental team to collect samples and a water truck to recover the fluid. During today's inspection, the elevated conductivity fluids were determined to have been removed and current fluid in the area was field measured for electrical conductivity at ~890us/cm. Based on the analytical sample results from sample #0983-421 and Repsol's timely response for remediation, violations of the following are cited as immediately corrected against API #015-23838:35 P.S. 691.402(b)35 P.S. 6018.30125 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)The DEP recommends the following:-Recovering the fluid held within the produced water tanks' secondary containment-Recovering the fluid held within the produced water tanks' smaller offload containment-Conducting necessary earth work to return the two smaller leveled surfaces near the entrance to pre-construction conditions and seeding/temporarily stabilizing No additional violations are cited at this time. I departed the site at 1045 hours.

Violation ID: 8209073
Permit API: 059-28368
Unconventional: No

Municipality: Center Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/18/2024
Comments: On 11/18/2024, I conducted an inspection of the Hunters Cave 3 OG Well in Center Township, Greene County in response to a diesel spill reported to the Departments Emergency Hotline on 11/18/2024 (CTS #385283). The spill, reported by EQT, stated that approximately 25 gallons of diesel fuel had spilled on the Hunters Cave 3 OG Well Pad while a contractor was changing out a fuel filter. The report stated that no impacts to Waters of the Commonwealth occurred, and SPSI were on site conducting spill remediation.While on site, I spoke to a contractor with SPSI who stated that SPSI estimated the diesel fuel spill was approximately 50 gallons. SPSI utilized a PID meter to obtain VOC measurements of the impacted area. At the time of inspection, SPSI was actively excavating impacted aggregate and indicated that some areas within the delineated spill remained above 5 ppm. Further excavation would occur to achieve VOC readings below 5 ppm. SPSI planned to backfill the excavation once readings were below 5 ppm. While on site, I observed the following:-The Hunters Cave 3 OG Well Act 9 sign was located at the site entrance. A mailbox containing Emergency Response Plans (ERP), site plans, and a well permit was located at the site entrance (Photos 1-2).-The site entrance and access road appeared to be in generally good condition (Photo 3).-The diesel spill was located on the left side of the pad, outside of the perimeter of the sound barriers installed along the pad. The excavated area was approximately 20 ft x 20 ft, with a depth of 2-4 inches. SPSI was actively excavating impacted material at the time of inspection, and a PID meter was used to obtain VOC readings within the excavation (Photos 4-6).-A rolloff box was staged across from the spill, containing impacted aggregate that was excavated by SPSI. I observed a strong diesel fuel smell being emitted from the impacted aggregate (Photos 7-8).-Two pad stormwater drains, located approximately 150 feet below the spill, did not appear to contain diesel fuel. I observed inlet protection within both stormwater drains (Photos 9-10).-The well pad slopes on either side of the diesel fuel spill appeared to be in good condition, and I observed no indication that the diesel fuel spill exited the gravel pad (Photos 11-12).-A drilling rig was staged on site at the time of inspection (Photos 13-14).Due to the diesel fuel spill release exceeding 42 gallons (1 barrel), violations of 78.54, 91.34(A), and SWMA 301 are being issued to the Hunters Cave 3 OG Well.

Unconventional: Yes

Comments: This inspection report has been developed to document an on-site routine complete inspect, and to summarize the overall status of this well and well location. The project was recently acquired by Big Dog Energy, LLC. Applications for the transfer of all four wells permitted on the site, from Geopetro LLC to Big Dog Energy LLC, were received by the Department on August 2, 2021. An application for the transfer of the ESCGP that is currently active on the site was also received by the Department. The current Operator information has not yet been updated in the Department's electronic database. Well number 019-21993, along with three other wells, (API ID#'s: 019-21988, 019-21992, 019-22002), were drilled and currently exist on the location. Although the act nine sign has been changed to reflect the current owner of the well location, the well tags have not yet been updated. Updated well tags should be installed on each of the wells at some point in the near future. Inspection ID number's 2762573 and 2762664, (conducted in early August 2018), suggest that only well number 019-22002 was ever stimulated. Additionally, it was indicated that, at the time, RE Gas intended to plug all four wells beginning with the three that had not been stimulated. The wells were never plugged. An inspection dated 07/26/2018 (ID#:2769196) cites violations for failure to restore the well location, 78a65(a)1i and OGA3216(A). ESCGP number ESX12-019-0148 is currently active on the site. The permit was renewed by RE Gas in 2017 and is set to expire on 07/17/2022. None of the earthwork proposed in the plan was ever implemented in the field. The location consists of one very large well location and a separate tank pad. The location is overgrown and clearly has not been tended to in any way for some time. There are currently, however, no clear E&S or stabilization-related issues associated with the site.

Comments: On 04/04/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 Well Site following violations issued on 12/08/2023 (IR 3657799, Enforcement 419234). On 12/08/2023, violations of 102.11(a), 102.22(a)2ii, and 78.53 were issued as outstanding for the access road. Inspection from 12/28/2023 noted that the violations were still open, however the operator was in compliance with schedule. On 01/24/2024, the violations were outstanding (IR 3701625). On 03/11/2024, the violations were issued as outstanding (IR 3726997). The operator was in compliance with schedule on 03/27/2024 (IR 3736262).The following was observed during inspection on 04/04/2024:Inspection conducted after several large rain events. The beginning upper part of the channel was displaying accelerated erosion and rills entering the channel (Photos 1, 2). The opposite side of the road was displaying accelerated erosion and sedimentation. Sediment accumulation was noted within the stabilized area with establishing vegetation (Photos 3, 4). Upper culvert inlet was blocked with sediment (Photo 5).Several sections of the bank above the channel did not have temporary stabilization. A section of open soils was displaying rills leading into the channel. The channel was also displaying accelerated erosion and sedimentation (Photos 6, 7).The middle culvert was completely blocked with sediment. Gravel was noted above the inlet, flowing over towards the channel. Debris and channelization were noted leaving the culvert inlet (Photos 8-10).The outlet of the middle culvert had sediment accumulation within the grass and accelerated erosion below (Photos 11-15).Outlet of roadside channel was displaying accelerated erosion and sedimentation. It was noted that sediment and flow were also both coming from the direction of the Landowner's building, in addition to the site's channel. Sediment accumulation within vegetation leading to the collection box and the site's middle culvert (Photos 16-20).Sediment accumulation within culvert and the outlet. This leads towards the stream (Photos 21, 22).Several rills leading off site and towards the roadside channel near the beginning section of the access road (Photos 23, 24). Remnants of gravel/sediment noted leading off the beginning of the access road towards the main township road (Photo 25).The violations issued on 03/11/2024 remain outstanding. A violation of 102.22(b)1 is being issued for the lack of temporary stabilization and the associated accelerated erosion.

Comments: During a routine inspection (ID 3840906) on 9/30/24 puddles were observed on the pad surface. The puddles were screened for conductivity and showed readings between 5 millisiemens per centimeter (mS/cm) and 7 mS/cm.Due to the elevated conductivity, sample 0719-286 was collected and analyzed by the DEP laboratory in Harrisburg. The sample results showed the presence of barium at 83.3 milligrams per liter (mg/L), strontium at 54.5 mg/L, chloride at 1643.4 mg/L, total dissolved solids at 3666 mg/L, and conductivity at 5.190 mS/cm.Based on the sample results, the following additional violations are being cited: SWMA 301, 78a56(a), and 78a66(b)1. A violation of CSL 402(b) was originally cited in inspection 3840906.Due to the unknown volume of released fluid, it is again recommended that Chesapeake pursue remediation under Act 2 requirements.

Comments: On August 25, 2025, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to the previous on-site inspection (IR 4031976), the Operator's update that excavation is complete (IR 4036853) and the NOV Response (IR 4036859).Act 9 sign is present. Emergency Response Plan (ERP) is on-site in the mailbox. Well head is tagged. No spills, leaks, or releases are observed at the well at this time. Empfield called back and informed the Department that environmental personnel could not be reached at this time but will keep trying (12:53).Excavated areas across the access road appear to remain unchanged since the previous inspection and remain covered in plastic. Empfield called back second time to inform the Department that the Operator is shutting down operations for the day until environmental personnel can be reached to assess the situation (1:18pm). The Operator is voluntarily shutting down operations as the Department did not request or order the Operator to do so. Based on today's inspection, all issued violations remain outstanding.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/26/2024
Comments: On April 26, 2024, the Department conducted a routine inspection of the Corbett 1 Well Pad located in Derry Township, Westmoreland County. Accompanying on todays inspection was Adam Clark (WQS DEP). At the time of the inspection, the Act 9 Sign was at the entrance of the access road and the ERP and PPC plans were in the onsite mailbox. The access road appeared stabilized and 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with no sedimentation or erosion issues was observed.Upon inspection of the well pad, the GPUs appeared equipped for production and no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed. The GPUs were not in secondary containment, however these wells have a SPUD date prior to the October 2016 promulgation of Chapter 78a. The Department still recommends that GPU units and other primary containments that contain regulated substances are stored within secondary containments to mitigate risk of discharge to the ground and Waters of the Commonwealth.The production tanks were within secondary containment and appeared heavily rusted in spots near the top. The Department recommends the Operator assess the integrity of the production tanks to ensure holes do not form in the top or side of the tanks. A wooden pallet was observed floating within the high level of water within the production tanks secondary containment and vegetation was observed to be growing all through the containment as well. During IR 3488331, the Department recommended the Operator keep all secondary containments dry and prevent the growth of vegetation within them. As the observations in IR 3488331 appear to be similar and/or unchanged from today's inspection, it does not appear that the Operator is maintaining the storage capacity of the secondary containment. The Department is requesting the Operator submit the past 12 months of secondary containment inspections within 3 business days of receipt of this inspection report.The well pad has three wells on it, this one being 8H (SPUD 11/28/2011), as well as 6H (SPUD 11/28/2011), and 4H (SPUD 11/28/2011). The 8H well appeared equipped for production and no observable fluid leaks or fluid discharges were seen. The well tag was posted and attached to the wellhead with all required information on it. Along the perimeter of the well pad, black tubing was observed laying on the ground, the Department is recommending the Operator remove all production equipment not currently in use. Based on todays inspection, violations shall be issued for the production tanks insufficient holding capacity and future violations may be forthcoming for failure to remove production equipment not currently in use.

Comments: The operator contacted the Department on Monday, September 16 to report a spill that was found at the Warrant 5573 W87 well site. This site was previously impacted by a 10+ barrel spill that occurred 8/4/16 (ID #2509096). The operator at the time, SWEPI LP, has since sold the well to Pennhills Resources, who is currently operating the well. SWEPI LP is remediating the site under the Department's Oil and Gas Spill Policy. Present on site for this inspection were DEP ECB representative Barry Stanton, Pennhills Resources' Stuart and Tom Morris, and SWEPI LP's Pat Bernethy, and myself. An unknown, but likely small, volume of oil leaked from a line at the site and leached down through rock and into a seep on the hillside below. A small amount of oil was visible in two siphon dams constructed as containment just below the site, as well as in a channel leading to a previously constructed siphon dam. A small amount of this oil was found leaking into an UNT of a Chappel Fork that was previously impacted. The total length of impact from the spill site is approximately 400 horizontal feet. The operator has dug up the line to determine where the leak occurred, and is collecting oil on absorbent pads. Discussion was made regarding the responsibility of each party regarding remediation and reporting. Further inspection will be done on this site as necessary.

The weather was 82 degrees F with partly cloudy skies. The inspection was conducted in response to a release reported by the operator. Complaints Tracking System (CTS) ID #390186 is tied to this reported release within CTS.Repsol reported to the DEP reporting hotline that on 6/30/2025 at ~0515 hours a failed gasket on a poly line caused a release of ~20 gallons of produced water to the pad surface, outside of secondary containment. An area estimated at 8 feet by 10 feet was impacted. According to Repsol, Resource Environmental was onsite 6/30/2025 to screen the area and oversee excavation efforts. Additional screening and excavation was scheduled to be completed later in the day on 7/1/2025. The poly line with the gasket that failed can be seen in photo #1. During my inspection, a representative with Repsol showed me the impacted area. I field measured some pooled fluid within the impacted area for electrical conductivity which returned a reading of ~12.67mS/cm. I also field measured pad material within the impacted area which returned readings ranging from 0.8 to 2.4mS/cm. Photo #2 shows the area that was impacted before remediation was completed. A Repsol representative later provided me photos of the area after remediation was complete via email. Resource Environmental confirmed through onsite screening that the release was cleaned up to visible. Photos #3 and 4 (provided by Repsol) show the area after remediation was completed.Based on the reported release of ~20 gallons of produced water to the pad surface and Repsol's timely remedial response, violations of the following are cited as immediately corrected against API #015-23890:Clean Streams Law 402(b)Solid Waste Management Act 30125 Pa.
